algorithm: Seeded shuffle of options; simulated test taker with configurable accuracy

complexity: O(q) per session over q questions
data_flow_ascii:
question bank -> seeded option shuffle -> Quiz

results -> score/total -> grade -> printed breakdown
description_sentence: A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.
failure_note: An out-of-range answer index raises ValueError at construction; interactive mode re-prompts on invalid input instead of crashing.

label: quiz engine
output_shape: Prints a per-question breakdown (chosen option, correct/wrong) plus score, percentage, and letter grade.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that quizzes you with shuffled options, scores every answer, and grades the result.

qa.a: The option order is shuffled with the seeded RNG and the correct index is remapped, so position carries no information.
qa.q: How do you stop the answer always being option 1?

qa.a: run_auto answers each question correctly with probability accuracy, using a dedicated RNG so the demo is reproducible.
qa.q: How does the auto-answered demo work?

qa.a: A/B/C/D/F at 90/80/70/60 percent cutoffs, computed from score over total questions.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python with deterministic option shuffling, auto and interactive answering modes, and letter-grade scoring.
run_notes: --interactive answers the quiz via input(); --accuracy and --num-questions tune the auto-answered demo.
scaling_note: In-memory question bank; fine for hundreds of questions, no database or multi-user session support.
storage_note: In-memory only: questions, answers, and scores exist only for the run and are printed, not saved.
tradeoff_note: A fixed built-in bank keeps the demo self-contained; a real quiz product would load questions from files or a database.
